Let me also give you the SON of JSON, which I am the developer of, version:

Q: How to replace a JSON value in Play A:

I'm considering moving away from all of those immutable "JSON" solutions. It's just making the code a horrible mess. This is how it would look in SON of JSON, which I am the developer of:

import nl.typeset.sonofjson._

val json = …
if (json.customerId.as[Int] == -1) {
  json.customerId = 987938
}

Q: Multiple devs pushing to same change A:

If multiple devs are pushing to the same patchset perhaps gerrit isn't the right tool for you. In any case multiple devs pushing the same patch in production code is a big no no. Just don't do it. There is a reason gerrit makes this difficult. What you really need is plain old github and have multiple devs push to the same branch (not master God forbid). This way you can git pull the latest commit on the branch rebase onto it. Once you have verified the code on the branch is correct make a pull request to master.

For production code you make a patch for a single dev and the patch has a single topic. Preferable a few dozen lines. Not more than 100 lines.

If you really must have multiple devs working on the same patchset on multiple machines(For example a single dev working on the same patch from multiple machines), here is how you do it.

Machine B is ahead of Machine A. The code in machine B is push to gerrit. In machine B get the latest commit number:

git log -1

Get the commit-id

Now type

git ls-remote origin "refs/changes/*/*" | grep commit-id

You will get

commit-id        refs/changes/aa/bbbb/cc

Now switch to machine A and make sure you local changes are commited (`git commit --amend`):

git fetch origin refs/changes/aa/bbbb/cc && git rebase FETCH_HEAD

Now git add . and resolve conflicts if you have any in the way you would in a regular rebase
